The nilpotent operator, taken from the bulk itself, links the full global conformal symmetry action, tying the radial effect to global symmetry.
arxiv-2605-08017:
Young Jo and two co-authors map how AI coding agents share work with humans across the life of a pull request. Two questions shape oversight: who initiates the work, and who authorizes its completion. Characterizing five tools on a collaborator-assistant spectrum, they analyze nearly thirty thousand pull request lifecycles through a taxonomy of initiator and approver roles.

Collaborator tools concentrate initiative in agents that open and carry the work, while assistant tools keep direction with humans and help in bounded ways. Across the whole spectrum, merge authority stayed almost exclusively human even where agents initiated nearly all the work. One blind spot recurs: where automation executes a merge, the logs name the executor but not the decision-maker. The paper contributes the taxonomy, per-tool state machines, and a replication package.
arxiv-2605-08217:
Rishi Ahuja, Kumar Prateek, Simranjit Singh, and Vijay Kumar challenge a habit that time series forecasting borrowed from language modeling: feeding ever longer history. In noisy, stochastic series, distant history is often volatility rather than signal, and attention may fail to ignore it.

On the ETTh1 benchmark, the authors find an inverse scaling pattern: error grows as context lengthens, and a three thousand step window degrades performance by more than two thirds. Their retrieval alternative, RAFT, keeps a fixed modest window and selectively fetches relevant past segments, beating both long-context models and the continuous architectures tested. The lesson is to retrieve, not to stuff.
arxiv-2605-08317:
Junkai Zhang, Hang Guo, Luca Benini, and Yawei Li unify two ways of shrinking the key-value cache that slows long-context language model inference. The cache grows with every token and is re-read at each decoding step, so serving long inputs is bound by memory, not arithmetic. Prior work either evicts tokens or quantizes them, rarely both.

Casting compression as a rate-distortion problem shows eviction and quantization are two ends of one bit-allocation scheme. Their RDKV method scores each token and channel by the distortion its compression would cause in attention, then hands out bits accordingly. Joint allocation squeezes the cache harder for the same quality loss.
arxiv-2605-08517:
Andreas Maier, Md Hasan, Paulina Conrad, and Paula Andrea Perez-Toro estimate the risk of deep networks that mix learned layers with fixed known operations. Their estimator splits total risk layer by layer, where known operations add nothing and learned layers add terms that shrink as training data grows. Replacing a learned layer with a known one always lowers the bound.

A medical scan example compares an operator aware rebuild method with one giant learned layer, and the predicted size ratio matches the true structure. Tests on small and medium images track real error closely. Builders of physics aware networks gain a tool for judging when hard coded knowledge truly helps.
arxiv-2605-08817:
Yifan Xu, Junren Chen, and Yifan Chen improve how language models learn to reason from checkable rewards. Sparse rewards over long reasoning chains make exploration hard, and training often collapses onto a narrow set of successful paths, raising single try accuracy without widening coverage. Their IMAX framework trains a pool of soft prefixes, small trainable prompts that each tilt the same base model toward a distinct style of reasoning rollout.

An information maximizing reward joins the verifiable reward to push the prefixes toward diverse, task relevant behaviors instead of noisy wandering. The method plugs into existing pipelines unchanged, and across three model sizes it lifts multi try success by clear margins. Reasoning training gains exploration by design at the start, not by accident.
arxiv-2605-08917:
M. Caldas and seven coauthors describe BOCOSUR, an all sky fireball camera network spread across Uruguay and built with school participation. Twenty autonomous stations, spaced widely over a large area, watch for bright meteors massive enough to drop recoverable meteorites, determine their incoming orbits, and seek links to parent asteroids. Deployment ran from 2019 to completion in 2023, with one major camera upgrade to a more sensitive, higher resolution system along the way.

The team compares both camera generations for position and brightness accuracy, and validates a method for measuring very bright fireballs against Jupiter and the full Moon. A fireball near peak magnitude minus nine, caught by four stations, demonstrates the network in action.
arxiv-2605-09017:
Arjan Cornelissen, working with two co-authors, Amin Shiraz Gilani and Subhasree Patro, asks how hard it is for a quantum computer to find short paths and cycles hidden inside a larger graph. Their 2026 study works in the adjacency matrix model, where the machine learns about a graph only by asking questions about it. Variants cover directed and undirected graphs, exact and bounded lengths, and promises about graph structure.

Sorting these variants by relative difficulty, the authors group them into equivalence classes using randomized reductions. For path problems they prove a sharp split: some need only a linear number of queries, while the rest match each other in difficulty. For the harder class they give a new quantum walk algorithm that beats the best earlier bound, plus a conditional lower bound tied to graph collision. Readers gain a clear map of which containment questions quantum methods can speed up.
arxiv-2605-09317:
LV-NUS Lab presents latent-memory-native GUI agents that carry visual, procedural, and task evidence forward beyond the current screen. Most agents still keep memory outside the policy as readable records: histories are summarised, retrieved, and reinserted as text before the policy encodes them again.

That split mismatches how modern GUI policies act, over latent sequences rather than symbolic records, so Mem-W treats memory as continuous context, not an auxiliary scaffold. A shared trajectory-to-latent compressor weaves past trajectories (experiential memory) and in-session segments (working memory) into compact tokens, joined with current observations into one embedding sequence. Self-distillation and outcome-aware supervision train Mem-W to keep decision-relevant state while sifting memory for evidence that truly supports task success. On four web and mobile navigation tests, Mem-W beats diverse backbones and memory-enhanced baselines, gaining up to 30 point 0.
arxiv-2605-09617:
An and four colleagues construct symmetric Sudoku type games from perfect codes. Their method uses the tiling property of Lee distance codes and diameter codes that are perfect to define subgrid constraints, so the resulting games inherit Sudoku's symmetry. They analyze two small cases in detail: a 5 by 5 Sudoku and an 8 by 8 Sudoku, defined over finite grids. Equivalence under rigid motions then gives a complete enumeration of valid grids.

For the 5 by 5 game they find 17 inequivalent solutions. For two types of 8 by 8 game they count 232,735 and 304,014 inequivalent solutions. A human like solver checks practical playability, and the 5 by 5 games show a balanced spread of difficulty from easy to hard. The construction offers a viable alternative to traditional 9 by 9 Sudoku, grounded in coding theory rather than ad hoc design.
arxiv-2605-09717:
Germain took a broad method for estimating curves from data and stretched it to a new job: guessing a full spread of likely values, not just one best value. The general regularisation scheme already joined regression, density-ratio, and score estimation under one roof. Germain built one shared frame for those jobs and worked out a new estimator for conditional densities, with proof of how fast its error shrinks as data grows.

For computing, the paper uses Landweber regularisation, a gradient method stopped early, which runs more easily here than the classic Tikhonov method. In tests, the new estimator matched or beat the standard Nadaraya-Watson estimator in varied cases, including time-series models. The work gives users a sound, rival option when the whole spread of outcomes matters.
arxiv-2605-10317:
Sayan K Chaki gives knowledge graph embedding a firm base drawn from quantum theory. Knowledge graphs store facts as triples, such as head entity, relation, and tail entity. Embedding models learn continuous vectors for entities and relations. Past operator models treat each relation as an operator, but never asked what form such an operator must take. His 2026 paper answers that question.

Chaki names three axioms any sound relation operator must meet: linearity, trace preservation, and complete positivity. By the Kraus representation theorem, those axioms define a Kraus channel form, and most past operator models emerge as rank-one special cases. Extending to varied metric geometries via w-Kraus channels, he proposes KrausKGE. It handles one-to-many and many-to-many relations, supports multi-hop reasoning with no path encoders, and needs no norm limits. It beat strong baselines on many-to-many relations.
arxiv-2605-10517:
W.J.G. de Blok and nine colleagues take hydrogen emission-absorption studies beyond the Local Group. H i emission-absorption studies constrain spin temperature and phase structure of hydrogen gas, but were largely limited to the Milky Way and the Local Group. Their 2026 paper extends the technique to galaxies 7 to 22 Mpc away using MHONGOOSE data.

The authors search toward 56 sources in 21 of the 30 MHONGOOSE galaxies. They detect absorption in three cases: one sight line in NGC 289 and two in NGC 7424. Detection rates are 3 of 56 for the full sample and 3 of 31 for a sub-sample behind 14 low-inclination galaxies. Detections happen only where continuum flux and column density are both high, with optical-depth sensitivity as the main limit. For detections, spin temperatures and cold fractions are derived. Temperatures and line widths match Local Group measurements, but cold fractions run lower, a resolution effect.
arxiv-2605-10717: Capellera and three colleagues present U2Diffine, a diffusion model for multi-agent paths. It fills in missing trajectory parts as well as forecasting them. The model adds the likelihood of predicted noise to the usual denoising loss. It carries latent uncertainty into real positions with a first-order Taylor step, and ranks each generated scene with a Rank Neural Network. Tested on four sports datasets, it beats leading methods at both completion and forecasting.
arxiv-2605-11117:
Juan Diego Toscano, Zhaojie Chai, and George Em Karniadakis present GRAFT-ATHENA, a self-improving agentic framework for autonomous discovery and evolutionary numerical algorithms. Discovery can be modeled as choices that map physical problems to numerical solutions. But existing agentic frameworks treat each problem alone, with no shared base to store method experience across domains.

GRAFT projects choice spaces into factored trees where each method is a single path, cutting the parameter count from exponential to linear. Paths sit in a metric space as unique fingerprints, so each new problem draws on similar past ones. On standard physics-informed machine learning benchmarks, GRAFT-ATHENA nears machine precision, beating human and prior agentic baselines. Scientific AI builders get a framework that grows its own action space across domains.
arxiv-2605-11217:
John Halloran presents RAG-Pref, retrieval-augmented generation for preference alignment, a training-free alignment method for large language models. Standard algorithms post-train over ranked pairs. But they demand heavy compute while proving far less capable of adding refusal guardrails against recent agentic attacks.

RAG-Pref conditions on preferred and dispreferred samples to use contrastive information during inference. It is online and works with off-the-shelf kits. Paired with offline training, it enables more than an average three point seven factor gain in agentic attack refusal cases across five widely used LLMs. That beats two point nine for other online methods and one point five for offline alone. It also improves general human-preference alignment without much raising compute. Builders get refusal guardrails that work at run time.
arxiv-2605-11317: Cheng and five colleagues propose SOMA, a cheaper way to serve large language models across multi-turn chats. Standard serving re-sends the full chat history each turn, which costs latency, memory and money. SOMA learns from early turns to map the local response space, then adapts a smaller surrogate model to that region for the rest of the chat. Soft prompts, anti-degeneration control and localized fine-tuning let the small model run alone, with a gate that can switch back on drift.
arxiv-2605-11617: Pham and five colleagues present MIST, streaming trees for online class-incremental learning. Streaming trees suit continual learning with local updates, yet fail in class-incremental settings from two miscalibrations: split criteria grow unreliable as classes expand, and no knowledge transfers at splits. Information gain scaling with class count forces Hoeffding-style radii to grow. MIST uses a K-independent McDiarmid radius for Gini splitting, a protocol passing parent statistics down, and leaf quantile sketches. On tabular streams it matches global methods and stays robust where rivals collapse.
arxiv-2605-11717: Yuri Kabanov and Artur Sidorenko study the stochastic Mayer control problem for financial markets with proportional transaction costs, framed geometrically through price processes and solvency cones. They examine how the optimal value and the optimal control behave when prices are approximated, proving continuity results in a general multi-asset setting. The work extends set-valued techniques for no-arbitrage, hedging, and portfolio choice to this control problem.
arxiv-2605-11917: Or Cohen, Alon Amar, and Ronen Talmon propose SERCOM, a Riemannian-aware method for spatial power estimation in array processing. Old methods measure straight-line gaps between sample and model covariance tables, ignoring that such tables live on the curved manifold of Hermitian positive definite tables. Using the Jensen-Bregman LogDet divergence, which needs no eigen-decomposition, SERCOM proved robust to spectral distortions. It beat existing methods on direction-of-arrival and power estimation, especially at low signal-to-noise ratios.
arxiv-2605-12017: Xinyi Zhang and Manuel Günther propose FAME, an explanation method combining activation mapping with perturbation ideas for image classification and face recognition. Class activation mapping assumes feature map locations reflect only underlying regions, an assumption that fails for deeper networks. FAME instead uses network gradients to manipulate the input image directly rather than applying fixed patches. Tests showed its attribution maps compete with state-of-the-art systems on both tasks.
arxiv-2605-12217: Michelangelo Barocci and three colleagues build a heterogeneous system-on-chip joining an open-source recurrent spiking network accelerator with standard processors. Spiking networks mimic brain-like spike processing with low power and parallel compute, but tape-out costs slow open hardware, so FPGAs offer a cheaper path. Their design runs ReckOn, a recurrent spiking accelerator, through the X-HEEP microcontroller and an ARM processor in Zynq Ultrascale systems. FPGA tests reproduce the taped-out ReckOn classification results, checking accuracy and physical traits, plus online learning on Braille digits.
arxiv-2605-12517: Kim and three colleagues fix a deployment gap for vision-language models used on text alone. Removing the image input causes large accuracy drops and severe miscalibration, and the model no longer behaves like its original language backbone. Missing meaning alone does not explain the failure: even text that preserves key content leaves confidence unreliable, while generated images partly restore performance. Their Latent Imagination Module predicts imagined latent embeddings from text through cross-attention, feeding a frozen backbone without synthesising pixels. It improves accuracy and calibration across text-only tests.
arxiv-2605-12617: Guo and four colleagues slim generative recommendation with simple MLPs. Recommenders use Semantic IDs, yet beam-expanded decoding makes inference slow. Prediction gets much easier after the first token, so repeated attention work is largely wasted. Their SID-MLP captures user context in one step, then distils the heavy teacher into MLP heads, cutting attention cost while keeping quality.
arxiv-2605-12717: Baharav and three colleagues study a collective linear ranking rule treating voter types proportionally. Each item's rank follows its score under a fixed vector, and each voter type prefers its own. The default arithmetic mean of preferred vectors is severely majoritarian. Surprisingly, the angular mean satisfies long-run proportionality: each type agrees with rankings in proportion to its share. Exact per-batch proportionality is impossible for linear rules, but its gap from long-run proportionality shrinks with batch size.
arxiv-2605-13217: Zhu and colleagues offer GAGPO, a training method for language model agents working over many turns. Agents often earn only a final reward, so credit for each step is hard to assign. GAGPO builds a grouped value proxy from sampled runs and pushes outcome signals back through time. Tests on two agent benchmarks show it beats strong baselines and learns faster early on.
arxiv-2605-13317: Boruah, Acharjee and Saikia model spin flow across an altermagnet and Ising superconductor junction with a spin active edge. Spin orbit coupling, uneven spin texture and edge scattering together shape charge and spin flow. Weak mixing keeps flow mostly helicity conserving with strong angular dependence, while strong mixing boosts spin filtering across a broad energy range. Spin filtering reaches about 86 percent, and flow turns directional, marking a tunable base for superconducting spintronics.
arxiv-2605-13517: Jaeyung Kim and YoungJoon Yoo propose ArcVQ-VAE, a spherical vector quantisation framework for learning discrete image representations. Vector quantised autoencoders tokenise whole images with a finite codebook, and that limit restricts how rich their codes can be. That prior joins ball-bounded norm regularisation, keeping codebook vectors inside a time-dependent ball, with an arc-cosine margin loss pushing latent vectors apart in angle. The result is more discriminative and evenly spread latent codes with better codebook use. Tests on reconstruction and generation show competitive accuracy and sample quality.
arxiv-2605-13617: Muneeba Mansha and Sarfraz Ahmad investigate the lcm-lattice of the edge ideal of a hypergraph. They establish conditions under which that lattice is Boolean, modular, or complemented. They extend the results to products of lcm-lattices in the complemented case. They also study how polarisation affects the lcm-lattices of an edge ideal and its polarised ideal.
arxiv-2605-13817: Bethel Hall and William Eiers show that large word models, fitted with an SMT solver, can audit software specs by turning them into formal logic. The team presents VERIMED, a neuro-symbol pipe running this idea for medical-device software specs. In counter-case-guided repair on a kidney-care Q and A test, SMT counter-cases raise verified hits from 55.4 percent to 98.5 percent. Over wide tests on open-source kidney-care safety specs, VERIMED reduces fuzz-prone specs and enables strict checks through SMT-based queries.
arxiv-2605-13917: Garvardt and Komusiewicz study correlation clustering, where vertices must be partitioned so that heavy edges stay inside clusters and light edges fall between them. The decision problem is fixed-parameter tractable in cost, but a polynomial kernel was thought unlikely. They show such a kernel exists when the cost is combined with the degeneracy, or alternatively the closure, of the fuzzy edge graph formed by weight-zero edges.
arxiv-2605-14017: Von Fellenberg, Labaj and Ressler aim to bound the dark cluster at the Galactic Center with future ELT and MICADO observations. The center holds the densest star crowd in the Milky Way, ruled by the black hole Sgr A* and its nuclear star cluster. Theory says many unseen stellar remnants, black holes, neutron stars and white dwarfs, should lurk there too. Their spread and traits shape mass segregation, cluster motion and the rate of extreme mass ratio inspirals for LISA.
arxiv-2605-14217: Lanpouthakoun and six co-authors propose PreFT, prefill-only tuning for fast inference. Large language models can now be tailored with parameter tuning, but serving user adapters harms speed, even with special kernels and memory handling. Prefill processes many tokens at once, while decode generates one token at a time, so decode runs far slower with many adapters. PreFT uses the adapter on prefill tokens only and discards it, lifting speed with minimal effect on performance. On 512 adapters for Llama 3.1 70B, PreFT reaches 1.9 times the speed of standard adapters.
arxiv-2605-14717: Nazir and Behera present a unified deep learning framework that reads white blood cell types and protein expression straight from label-free differential phase contrast images, without fluorescent staining. A hybrid design fuses convolutional texture features with transformer-based global features through a learnable cross-branch gate. A language model then writes short biologically grounded summaries of predicted cell states. On two benchmarks, white blood cell accuracy near ninety-one percent and a CD16 correlation of 0.72 are reported.
arxiv-2605-14817: Shapiro studies when the spectral curve of a finite pencil of Jacobi matrices is reducible. The pencil adds a diagonal matrix to a tridiagonal matrix with zero main entries, scaled by a parameter. Generic irreducibility is proved when entries are pairwise distinct. Several basic reducibility mechanisms are given, including disconnected Jacobi chains, constant eigenvalue branches, mirror-symmetric parts, and scalar blocks. A conjecture on reducibility is stated, with low-size evidence and counterexamples to optimistic claims.
arxiv-2605-14917: Leonardo Ferreira Guilhoto, Akshat Kaushal, and Paris Perdikaris tackle active learning for regression when predictions split into several modes. Variance misses disagreement between modes, and standard information measures suit discrete outputs, not continuous ones. Their Two-Index framework separates doubt about which model is right from randomness inside each model. From it they derive a Mutual Information Lower Bound rule that, on multi-mode benchmarks, matched or beat every baseline tested.
arxiv-2605-15117: Arshay Sheth proves that the x-axis is the only real algebraic curve whose image under the Gamma function stays inside an algebraic curve. The argument adapts a base-change technique of Tamiozzo. It carries a complex geometric transcendence result of Eterović, Padgett, and Zhao into the real setting. As an application, Sheth combines the real and complex results. They study analogues of the Manin-Mumford conjecture for the Gamma function, which concerns intersections of curves with special point sets.
arxiv-2605-15317: Richard Evan Schwartz proves a result about discrete faithful representations of the modular group into isometries of SL(3,R)/SO(3). With the order-two generator fixed-point unique, their space has a Barbot component homeomorphic to the plane crossed with a half-line. The boundary of this component parametrizes Pappus representations, geometric configurations tied to Pappus's theorem, while the interior consists of Anosov representations, dynamically well-behaved actions. The result maps the boundary between two representation worlds.
arxiv-2605-15417: Jake Fawkes and Jason Hartford widen a low-variance loss for generative models. The old loss matched one divergence. Their new family spans all f-divergences. On-policy, each loss has gradients that match its own divergence. Off-policy, it keeps the same best answer. Designers can thus pick traits like wider coverage with no loss of the off-policy pledge. Tests span toy tasks, molecule search with SynFlowNets, and async tuning of large language models.
arxiv-2605-15517: William D. Compton, Zachary Olkin, and Aaron D. Ames train perceptive locomotion policies for humanoid robots whose reference paths are adjusted during training to match terrain geometry. Footsteps are projected onto valid footholds, and swing-foot and center-of-mass paths are reshaped accordingly, exposing a clean velocity interface for standard navigation planners. In simulation the terrain-aware references track better, and on a Unitree G1 robot the system navigated over 70 meters outdoors through rough ground and stair flights with all sensing onboard.
arxiv-2605-15617: Shaoke Xi and thirteen colleagues present PrismLLM, a system that emulates large-scale language-model training on only a few graphics processors. It builds a high-fidelity execution graph by slicing, capturing computation, communication, and dependencies at target scale, then runs selected ranks for real while replaying the rest as virtual participants. Experiments show average iteration-time error of only 0.58 percent and peak-memory error under 0.01 percent, emulating clusters up to 8,192 graphics processors with under one percent of the physical hardware.
arxiv-2605-15817: Esther Bosch, Klas Ihme and Stefan Bohmann ask which moments of a bus or train trip shape how travelers later judge it. They sampled on-trip experience every five minutes across 2576 real public transport trips in three German cities, then compared aggregation rules against post-trip satisfaction. A Minimum-End rule, combining the worst moment with the final experience, predicted best. Averages, peak-end rules, the final moment alone and trip length all fared worse. The authors suggest fixing bad moments and endings to lift remembered satisfaction.
arxiv-2605-15917: Boris Shapiro studies maps of convex polytopes to a line, spurred by the inverse moment problem. The Lebesgue measure on a convex d-shape gives spline curves of degree d-minus-1. Their moments lead to higher Prony systems, with the classic system regained at d-equals-0. Shapiro maps the fixed-knot spline cone and gives an exact amplitude recovery rule. He records the recurrence of the scaled moments. He links the directional moment variety to the Hankel determinantal variety of moment varieties on polytopes.
arxiv-2605-16117: Zhang and four colleagues introduce SGR, a step-by-step aid that grounds language-model thought in outside knowledge graphs. The model first builds a small graph shaped to the question, then thinks step by step over that graph and merges several thought paths. Tying each step to structured evidence helps it focus on the right entities, links, and support. Across several benchmarks, SGR beat strong rivals on both accuracy and factual reliability.
arxiv-2605-16317: Root, Mujo, and Xu develop a basic chance-based model for event camera sensing grounded in photon stats. The model unifies static scene noise events and step response curves, or S-curves, within one single tool, with exact Poisson, saddle-point, and Gaussian forms across brightness regimes. It clears up S-curve reading beyond fixed chance thresholds. Their Noise2Params method finds camera log-contrast threshold, lux-to-photon ratio, and leakage values from static uniform scene tapes alone, giving an easy tuning option.
arxiv-2605-16517: Kini and 17 others present Gemini for Google, a Gemini version for Google's software world. Company software work is an ongoing process of additions, edits, launches, and upkeep, making tuning data. The paper details work from a trillion-token dataset to a mid-training strategy mitigating catastrophic forgetting. In an A/B study across 29,000 developers, Gemini for Google outperformed baselines, reducing iterations per turn by 23 percent and increasing code survival by 17 percent. Beyond metrics, the paper provides a blueprint for company use covering signal extraction, data preparation, tuning, and downstream deployment.
arxiv-2605-16917: Thomson's team releases the second SPICE-RACS set, cutout spectra and polarisation for millions of sources from the Rapid ASKAP Continuum Survey. Covering 88 percent of the sky from the south pole to declination 49 degrees, it gives cubes in Stokes I, Q and U around four million and spectra for five million components. After removing duplicates, its polarisation catalogue holds 250 thousand Faraday rotation measures above eight sigma, the largest rotation-measure catalogue yet, about five times all earlier ones combined. All products are public through CSIRO archives.
arxiv-2605-17017: Agrawal, Jain and Nayyar make behaviour foundation models robust to dynamics shifts at inference time. Existing base models assume fixed dynamics, limiting robustness when friction, actuation, or sensor noise change. The authors recast task inference as robust minimax optimisation, adapting to worst-case shifts without touching pretraining. Their framework is the first base-model approach robust to shifts using only offline data from one environment. It beats standard base-model and robust offline imitation baselines under shifts, showing robust policies can come from inference.
arxiv-2605-17117: Hammond's 2026 study tests four geometry-flavored signals drawn from stock-index returns as warnings of market regime shifts. Against forty-six classic and machine-learning rivals across seventeen crises, one signal, the Berry phase rate, stands out, cutting false alarms by about two-thirds versus a supervised forest. Reduced state purity separates regimes best in-sample. Geometry and classic channels barely overlap, suggesting they track different risks.
arxiv-2605-17217: Strauss and Sharma build a quantum-assisted support vector machine ensemble that spots marine oil spills in radar satellite imagery pixel by pixel. Quantum annealing tunes weak classifiers on small data slices, which are then combined classically. On Sentinel-1 images it reaches 0.60 overlap with truth and 0.89 balanced accuracy, matching a strong classical baseline, and it transfers to independent spill images from the Strait of Hormuz.
arxiv-2605-17417: Yang and colleagues investigate a levitated ferromagnet lattice serving as a scalable sensor for ultralight dark matter, which would induce weak oscillating magnetic-like signals. They model the collective lattice response in the fully confined regime, including dipole-dipole interactions, finite-size corrections and boundary mode mixing. They also work out the noise budget. Those effects create only a narrow blind zone, and projected sensitivities beat single-ferromagnet detectors in all three coupling channels.
arxiv-2605-17617: Zhu and colleagues present GraphMind, which builds, runs and evolves workflow graphs from operational traces. An offline pipeline mines graphs of problems, actions and causal links from traces. An online engine walks the graph, mixing guided retrieval with language-model reasoning. Adaptive Traversal Reinforcement strengthens successful paths from feedback. Deployed on four cloud services and tested on 93 incidents, it beats a Summary-RAG baseline on reach, hallucination rate and throughput with eight times less context. A 12-week field study finds 97 percent of scored chats yield actionable results.
arxiv-2605-17817: D. G. C. McKeon and three colleagues build a quantum gravity model that stays both renormalizable and unitary. A Lagrange multiplier field caps quantum corrections to the Einstein-Hilbert action at one-loop order. That cap yields a model that is renormalizable and unitary, yet still reproduces the Einstein field equations in the classical limit. The result is a tight, minimal account: one added field tames the quantum corrections without breaking the classical theory it extends.
arxiv-2605-18217: Henrik van Impel's 2026 study maps carbon monoxide in three dimensions above a micro cavity plasma array run at atmospheric pressure. Combining TALIF imaging with an ICCD camera, the team resolves CO densities above the discharges that generate the gas from carbon dioxide in helium. The measured clouds match a basic 3D diffusion model well, and flow tests show a laminar, Poiseuille-like profile inside the reactor. Local dissociation near 40 percent saturates CO output as voltage rises, marking a useful platform for plasma catalysis work.
arxiv-2605-18317: Hugo Le Du's 2026 paper tunes doping in niobium diselenide sheets through misfit layer compounds. These compounds stack rocksalt and dichalcogenide layers, offering control beyond plain gating. By alloying lanthanum and lead in the rocksalt layer, the team shifts doping exactly. Density functional theory plus angle-resolved photoemission shows the rocksalt unit acts as a donor. Varying the lanthanum-lead ratio shifts the Fermi level rigidly while keeping the monolayer's structure and two-dimensional nature.
arxiv-2605-18517: Haoxiang Wan and Xingpeng Li propose, in a 2026 paper, a modular security-constrained unit commitment plan coordinating flexible data center workloads with system scheduling. Three models cover spatial shifting across sites, temporal shifting at each site, and joint spatio-temporal flexibility. On a modified IEEE 24-bus test system, the joint model wipes out all base-case and post-contingency violations at 40 percent flexibility. It also cuts renewable curtailment by up to 84.4 percent at 30 percent flexibility.
arxiv-2605-18617: Ziyu Wei and four co-authors present ManiSoft, a 2026 benchmark for vision-language control of soft continuum robots. A tuned sim pairs lifelike soft-body dynamics with contact-rich interaction via an elastic force constraint. Four tasks span gripper coordination to obstacle avoidance, backed by 6,300 generated scenes and expert paths from a planner plus reinforcement learning policy. Three policy models do well in clean scenes but drop sharply under randomization, failing mainly on visual estimates of body state.
arxiv-2605-19017: Khandaker Abrar Nadib, Marina Kogan, Alexander Lex and Maxim Lisnic test guard lines in charts that push a view. Such lines, set right in a chart, can blunt cherry picked data and sly captions that fool readers. Late fact checks land too late, since held views stick. In a planned study of COVID and stocks charts, guard lines raised trust, rank sense and full context sense.
arxiv-2605-19217: Michael Martinez surveys the most promising lensed radio sources for probing dark matter, whose tiny-scale nature remains one of cosmology's open questions. Dark halos bend light and shift image positions and brightness, so lens systems can separate rival particle models. Radio sources are scarce for this work, though their positions can be measured with great precision. He explains which lens traits matter most, reports two new searches in existing surveys, and weighs how complete the resulting population is.
arxiv-2605-19417: Innan, Rehman and Shafique bring order to quantum transfer learning claims for image classification, where past results varied in data, preprocessing, backbones and qubit budgets. They test five hybrid methods under one pipeline with frozen classical backbones and small trainable quantum heads, on Fashion-MNIST and an ants-versus-bees set, with CIFAR-10 as a harder check. No family wins everywhere: results hinge on dataset, encoding, circuit design and cost. The authors argue future comparisons must weigh resources, not accuracy alone.
arxiv-2605-19717: Berger and team propose a hybrid architecture putting validated engineering tools inside the decision loop of AI agents for CAD. Language models can generate computer-aided design yet lack physical sense for reliable engineering. Here design becomes a closed loop where agents plan, generate, evaluate and revise designs against a load case, using knowledge tools as feedback. The system also brings a benchmark dataset and metrics for working validity. It produces more complex, truly verified designs, raising complexity by 4 point 2 and compile rate by 3 point 5 percent over similar methods.
arxiv-2605-19817: Ito, Mameda and Yamamoto derive the spin Hall effect of gravitons from quantum field theory of linearised gravity. They build Wigner functions for right and left handed gravitons from second order metric perturbations in the energy momentum tensor. Berry curvature of opposite sign for the two helicities then splits the graviton energy Hall current by helicity. The splitting measures exactly twice the corresponding photon spin Hall current. The work gives a field theoretic account of how curved spacetime sorts gravitons by handedness.
arxiv-2605-20417: Davoudi's talk motivates quantum simulation of gauge theories for particle and nuclear physics. Lattice field theory excels on spectra, structure, decays and reactions, yet dense matter and general dynamics demand exponential classical time and space. Quantum methods promise polynomial-time algorithms instead, and lattice theorists now pursue theory, algorithms, hardware and co-design together. The talk reviews recent progress and closes on challenges and openings ahead.
arxiv-2605-20717: Ankit Kumar Tenwar, Mukul Lokhande, and Santosh Kumar Vishvakarma present E-ReCON, a compact compute-in-memory macro for edge AI. The 16-kilobit design uses a 3T1R ReRAM bitcell of only 0.85 square micrometres and supports in-memory multiplication for both standard and spiking neural networks. An interleaved adder tree cuts transistor count by 37 percent and power by 28 percent against a standard design. Built in 65-nanometre CMOS, it reaches up to 419 tera-operations per second per watt.
arxiv-2605-21217: Shuaida He, Liwen Chen, and Long Feng study federated LoRA fine-tuning of large language models via collaborative alignment. Low-rank adaptation enables parameter-efficient tuning across clients, but clients may share only partial structure and a substantial subset may be contaminated. Their CLAIR method, built only on preliminary local estimators, recovers the shared LoRA subspace and detects contaminated clients through a low-rank plus block-sparse decomposition. It applies broadly, from linear regression to neural network and language model modules, and proves exact recovery in the noiseless case.
arxiv-2605-21317: Ziqi Wang, Qiang Liu, and Nils Thuerey present CRAFT, a merging method for federated training under varied data. Naive averaging can improve the global goal while conflicting with specific clients and degrading them. CRAFT treats the global update as a geometric correction, finding the update closest to a reference direction subject to conflict-free alignment rules. A closed-form solution avoids iterative solvers, and layer-wise adaptation handles conflicts at varied feature scales. Theory shows CRAFT promotes a common-descent structure and mitigates conflicts via projection geometry.
arxiv-2605-21517: Meliksah Yorulmazlar argues for proactive archiving of the ephemeral web. The web is often treated as a lasting record of public and social life, yet in practice it is fragile, fluid, and often ephemeral. Domains change, rebuilds erase earlier material, institutions move, keepers graduate, and political unrest can cut digital access entirely. He motivates early saving through a case study of the Pakistan Embassy International School and College Tehran, whose domain, identity, leadership, and location all changed after his graduation.
arxiv-2605-21617: Eloïse Touron and co-authors present BlockFormer, a transformer-based method inferring genomic features from contact maps. Locating centromeres from Hi-C maps poses an inverse task: one parameter per entity must be inferred from a map of pairwise interactions grouped in blocks of varied number and size. Their model handles that variability, trained on abundant cheap synthetic data from a custom simulator. Applied to centromere localization, it recovers spots at or below map resolution across species with varied genome sizes.
arxiv-2605-21717: Arne Bouillon and Oliver Dunbar extend likelihood-informed subspaces to tempered Bayesian posteriors, annealed forms used when data are scarce. These subspaces keep only telling directions, but prove restrictive in practice. Their partly informed alpha-LIS spaces often reach near-optimal quality even when alpha falls below one. They also build extensions using data from the whole tempered sequence and simple gradient stand-ins for chaotic or stochastic systems. In experiments their full-sequence approach proves far more robust than the optimal alpha-equals-one choice.
arxiv-2605-21817: Emily Heath and Andrew Simmons bound the Z-p Ramsey number linearly for graphs with a 2-packing. With edges colored in Z-p, the Ramsey number is the smallest N forcing a copy whose edge colors sum to zero. This needs minimum degree at least one, a prime dividing the edge count, and a 2-packing of size p minus one. The number is at most n plus six p minus nine. It sharpens with packing vertex degrees, with equality. It gives n plus a constant for bounded-degree graphs.
arxiv-2605-21917: Han Zhang and co-authors present MAVEN, an agentic pipeline in several stages that converts raw video into structured training data for video event reasoning. Manual labeling cannot capture the what, when, where, why, and consequence of events at scale, so MAVEN chains agents that produce multi-task data with chain-of-thought traces. Training on its CCTV-only data lifts Cosmos-Reason2 by 10.7 points on AccidentBench and equals Gemini 2.5 Pro, despite seeing no dashcam video. Added dashcam data and reinforcement post-training push it past both Gemini baselines.
arxiv-2605-22017: Lei Chu and Yuhuan Zhao tackle multi-agent motion prediction, where forecasts must be both diverse and jointly consistent across interacting people. Deep generative models capture varied human behavior well, yet most are judged only by single-agent metrics that miss joint dynamics. Their context-guided diffusion method adds energy-based joint refinement, keeping each trajectory plausible while enforcing consistency across agents. Tests on four benchmarks beat existing methods, with large gains on both marginal and joint metrics on ETH/UCY over strong marginal baselines.
arxiv-2605-22517: Gen and team map the high-field phase diagram of cubic helimagnet SrFeO3 using magnetoelastic data. SrFeO3 hosts a fourfold-Q hedgehog grid, but its many-Q cause is open. The team shows how the diagram shifts with field direction and builds a spin model with cubic bias plus two-way and four-way links from spin-charge coupling. They see elastic signs of ligand-hole amount shifts on entry to the forced ferromagnetic phase. Charge flow from ligand-hole band buildup holds many-Q phases.
arxiv-2605-22617: Blanco and team hunt for radio polarization in WR 147 and HD 167971. PACWBs are massive star pairs where winds clash, speeding bits to high speeds. Their synchrotron radio glow should show linear polarization, but no sign has been seen for any PACWB. Both were watched with the Very Large Array in L and C bands. No sign was seen in either band, even narrow bands. The upper limit is about 1 percent for both. Lack of linear polarization likely comes from choppy fields, Faraday and beam effects, and heat.
arxiv-2605-22817: Bahlous-Boldi and eight colleagues propose Vector Policy Optimization, a way to train language models for varied answers rather than one narrow style. Usual training rewards a single score, which shrinks variety and weakens search at test time, when many candidate answers are tried. Their method trains against several reward signals at once, so different answers fit different trade-offs. Across four tasks it matched or beat strong single-reward baselines.
arxiv-2605-23017: Finocchiaro, Ganson, and Khurana study rough calibration for discrete traits of outcome distributions, such as the mode or rankings. Binary calibration extends poorly to multiclass settings, where prediction spaces grow exponentially with class count. Noarov and Roth eased that blowup by judging traits of the distribution instead, measured by elicitation complexity. Prior work covered mostly continuous scalar traits. The authors use Lipschitz continuous traits as go-betweens to handle discrete traits that are strongly orderable, and give algorithms for designing them.
arxiv-2605-23417: Klein and colleagues release BBO-Pile, the first open dataset for training foundation models for black-box optimization, where tuning is costly and methods often fail to transfer across domains. Earlier work leaned on private or purely synthetic trajectories, blocking reproduction and real-world use. BBO-Pile holds over 500000 trajectories across 3095 black-box problems and several optimizers. Models trained on it from 2 million to 80 million parameters show that large-scale pretraining can imitate optimization methods, opening the field to wider study.
arxiv-2605-23517: Stade proves a probabilistically checkable proof theorem for the existential theory of the reals, which asks whether real variables can satisfy polynomial constraints and inequalities. He shows MAX-ETR-INV resists approximation within a factor. MAX-ETR-INV seeks the largest satisfiable subset of constraints of forms x equals 1, xy equals 1, and x plus y equals z. Even non-deterministic polynomial-time algorithms cannot beat that factor unless the existential reals equal NP. He gives an 8-factor polynomial-time algorithm and a 2-factor non-deterministic one.
arxiv-2605-23617: Turek, Sun, and Yao propose multiphoton heralding with a parametric amp turning squeezed vacuum into two non-Gaussian groups: large squeezed Schrödinger cat states and parity Fock superpositions. Feeding m photons into the idler port and counting n at the output gives high-order removal. The output states show negative Wigner values and richness. Under photon loss, richness stays large even after negative values fade. The states beat the Heisenberg limit in phase sensing, making the device a platform for loss-proof metrology and fault-proof processing.
arxiv-2605-23817: Hashorva and Thäle show that in Poisson Boolean models with ball grains, the directional visible range from an uncovered point is exponential. This is known in Euclidean and real hyperbolic space, and they extend it to every simply connected non-compact homogeneous harmonic manifold. They also construct complete uneven Riemannian manifolds showing that exact exponentiality matches exact tube linearity. Superlinear tube growth leads to Weibull-type tails, while near tube linearity still yields an exponential decay rate.
arxiv-2605-24217: Chandrasekar and Kramberger show production benchmarks for language-model inference carry systemic measurement bias. Widely used tools run single-process clients whose queuing bottlenecks inflate first-token and per-output-token times as rates climb. Modelling the client as a queue, the authors trace distortion to the Python Global Interpreter Lock. They answer with a multi-process frame spreading client load so queuing overhead turns negligible, plus a normalized token-time metric for latency across sequence lengths. The method isolates serving performance at thousands of queries per second.
arxiv-2605-24317: Moradifam and Orozco-Fernandez study soundness of p-area smallest surfaces in the Heisenberg group under changes to the weight function and drift field in broad least-slope problems. Without strict curve, proving minima stay stable is hard. Under firmness and shape rules, they derive measured soundness bounds in both plain and first-slope norms for changes to the weight and drift apart. They further give joint bounds under changes to all three main inputs at once, weight, drift, and source term. Test runs show the soundness theory.
arxiv-2605-24717: Andrea De Domenico and others introduce refutation display calculi for basic lattice-based logics. Refutation calculi derive the invalid formulas of a logic, and while they shaped tableaux systems, no refutation approach to display calculi existed. The authors build such calculi for LE-logics, the logics of basic normal lattice expansions of any signature. They prove soundness and completeness through proof-analysis results on derivable sequents. Finally, terminating tableaux calculi follow from these refutation display calculi, closing a gap between refutation methods and display proof theory.
arxiv-2605-24917: Zhe Hu leads a model for why known neutron star masses cluster in two humps, a pattern whose origin is still debated. The team builds a super-Eddington model for neutron stars gaining mass from a companion. They run it through population synthesis to trace how masses grow. Growth turns on orbit period and donor mass, and the model reproduces both humps. The higher hump, just under twice the Sun's mass, comes mainly from light-donor short-orbit systems, while shared-envelope systems account for the lower hump.
arxiv-2605-25217: Mohamed Camil Belhadjoudja designs a backstepping controller for first-order hyperbolic equations with spatially varying coefficients in any dimension. A change of variables driven by the characteristic flow turns the full system into a continuum of decoupled one-dimensional systems, each moving along its own characteristic curve. A control is built for each one-dimensional system. The controls are then put back in the original frame. The result steadies the full system in finite time, provided curves foliate the domain with uniformly bounded transit times, the non-trapping condition.
arxiv-2605-25517: Rahul Vishwakarma, Shushant Kumar, and Ratnesh Jamidar ask what makes an answer engine cite one source first over another. They build a controlled two-document testbed injecting two candidate sources and measuring which earns the first citation marker. Across six models they run 252,000 trials, varying 18 content factors one at a time. Topical relevance and list position drive first citations most, with price and recent timestamps helping consistently. Completeness and trust cues help less, while formatting edits matter little. The team releases a reproducible protocol and prioritized checklist.
arxiv-2605-25717: Ribeiro and colleagues present FLOATBench, a benchmark for fatigue damage in floating offshore wind turbine towers. Most offshore wind resource lies in deep water, where floating turbines are essential. The benchmark holds over 580,000 fatigue labels across three tower shapes, drawn from nearly 20,000 high-fidelity simulations. A regime-aware partition splits test points across in-train, interpolation and extrapolation groups, exposing shifts random splits miss. Its three-level harness is the first tabular surrogate protocol for turbine fatigue.
arxiv-2605-26317: Simon Mataigne and P.-A. Absil build a fast Jacobi-style routine for eigenvalues, and optionally eigenvectors, of a real normal matrix. The trick leans on Paardekooper's method for skew-symmetric matrices. It pays best when most eigenvalues are complex, as with random orthogonal matrices from statistics on curved spaces, where it beats rival Jacobi-style routines. The paper also gives plain formulas for the nearest symmetric skew-Hamiltonian matrix and the nearest ortho-symplectic matrix.
arxiv-2605-26417: Deep Nath and three colleagues propose one Inefficiency Metric for spotting structural strain in the Hedera transaction network. They run principal component analysis and correlation matrices over six years of transactions, pulling out two near-independent axes. One is effective diameter, how far payments spread. The other is closeness centrality, how smoothly flows move. The metric swings with big economic events, rising with middleman splintering and falling when the network tightens under stress. It matches a seven-feature anomaly detector while staying easy to read.
arxiv-2605-26517: Yaoyu Zhang and six colleagues design joint positioning and communication for pinching antennas, which move antennas along a waveguide. Uplink positioning for indoor settings comes first, then downlink. Two scenarios assume line-of-sight channels and one user: single- and multi-antenna setups. Signal-strength ranging and least-squares positioning serve the single-antenna case. The multi-antenna case derives a closed-form signal sum and a grid algorithm. Results show smaller precision dilution cuts error, non-parallel waveguides help, and noise hits data rate twice over.
arxiv-2605-26617: Joydeep Naskar extends a holography rule about three-way quantum links from pure states to mixed states. The first rule ties leftover entropy to true three-way entropy and bars purely GHZ-like three-way links. Naskar first tries a minimal extension with reflected entropy, and finds shapes that break it when a Markov gap vanishes. Mirroring the recipe through a purified twin state restores the rule, and he conjectures a fresh rule for three-party states with supporting evidence.
arxiv-2605-26917: Angurel develops the theory of equivariant ultra Kolyvagin systems to bypass structural limits of the Euler system machinery over infinite rings. Using classes in exterior powers of patched Selmer groups, built from ultraproducts of classical Selmer groups, he computes an Iwasawa Selmer group up to pseudo-isomorphism. He proves it has no finite submodules. He applies the framework to the fine Selmer group of an elliptic curve and the Bloch-Kato Selmer group of a Rankin-Selberg convolution of modular forms.
arxiv-2605-27117: Li, Feng, and Sun argue alignment alone cannot guarantee AI safety in open settings. An aligned agent may refuse to yield to runtime authority under adversarial inputs or risky tool use. They define controllability as staying interruptible, overridable, redirectable, and constrainable by control signals. They introduce ControlBench, a benchmark for failures in agentic settings. Tests with OpenClaw agents show guardrails reduce risk yet fail to give enforceable runtime control. So they propose a control-first design built around control planes, intervention paths, and auditable interfaces.
arxiv-2605-27517: Jia Wei Teh, Ralf Klessen, Simon Glover, and Kathryn Kreckel introduce TRINITY, a thin-shell code coupling winds, radiation, and photoionised gas in molecular clouds. The code evolves bubble-shell structure under winds, supernovae, radiation pressure, ionized-gas pressure, and gravity, with cloud shapes from uniform to Bonnor-Ebert spheres. Ionized-gas pressure widens the shell radius by about 17 percent at 10 million years. Cloud shape decides if a cloud disperses, re-collapses, or leaks ionizing photons.
arxiv-2605-27617: Tom Verhoeff gives shorter deterministic solutions for the k-out-of-n picture-hanging puzzle in two regimes. For 2-out-of-n and for n-minus-2-out-of-n with n a power of two, his polynomial-length constructions improve on the earlier quasi-polynomial construction. Exhaustive search also fixes 16 as the shortest length for the 2-out-of-4 puzzle, reached by two structurally distinct solutions.
arxiv-2605-27717: Johan Garcia, Simon Sundberg, and Anna Brunstrom characterize Starlink queuing with high-precision burst-pattern traffic generation. Measuring one-way delay and loss against a queue simulator, they find Starlink uses neither per-flow fair queuing nor drop-tail buffers, but drop-front buffer management. Drop-front cuts delay yet may disturb loss-based congestion control assumptions, potentially degrading throughput.
arxiv-2605-27917: Kim and colleagues model drone intrusions as a contest between an attacking drone and a network of sensors guarding buildings. Their defender slides sensors freely along building edges rather than snapping them to fixed points, and both sides are optimized together toward a local Nash equilibrium. The result offers a deployable baseline for counter-drone sensor placement.
arxiv-2605-28017: Yin and colleagues retest prompt-injection tricks on product recommendation lists under true search pipelines, where a tainted page must first be fetched and ranked. Most tricks died before the text maker; only model-made injections lived through. A small guard model trained on attack cases caught each trick, hinting that today's threats can be spotted.
arxiv-2605-28317: Pranav Lakshmanan and Paras Chopra build neural surrogates for physics that fail loudly, not silently, at shocks and contacts. One network predicts any future state in a single pass, while its error map concentrates exactly on discontinuities, recoverable from forward passes alone. Gating a reference solver on that map halves residual error, with solo speedups of twenty-six to seventy-two times.
arxiv-2605-28517: Yunwen Lei, Zimeng Wang, and Xiaoming Yuan analyze whether stochastic gradient descent with momentum generalizes to unseen data. Momentum speeds training, but it was conjectured to harm generalization. They build a generalized framework covering Polyak and Nesterov momentum and prove tight on-average stability bounds for smooth convex problems. The bounds exploit small optimization errors along the path, cover any momentum below one, and need no Lipschitz assumption, yielding optimal excess population risk bounds for both schemes.
arxiv-2605-28617: Yaoyu Zhao and five colleagues present LACUNA, a model letting model-written code shape the agent runtime without giving up safety. Each agent action is a typed request the model fills with code when execution reaches it, checked against the surrounding program before running. Rejected actions leave the environment untouched, and compiler notes drive a retry, while the check limits which tools and data an action can touch. The primitive expresses ReAct loops, sub-agents, parallel decomposition, and joint planning as control flow, reaching 76 percent on 392 tau-2-bench tasks.
arxiv-2605-28717: Bojie Li presents OpenURMA, the first clean-room open implementation of Huawei's Unified Bus for datacenter RDMA. Current RDMA holds per-connection state for app-endpoint pairs and pays a four-step PCIe round trip on operations. Unified Bus splits app endpoint state from host transport state, makes ordering opt-in, and reaches remote memory via CPU load and store. Built at three tiers, from RTL on an Alveo U50 to simulators, its load path hits about 500 nanoseconds, about 4.4 times below baseline, with nearly three times higher throughput.
arxiv-2605-29417: Deokmin Hwang presents ParCo-SDF, a two-stage method for partial-to-complete signed distance field reconstruction of soft objects. Recent methods use hidden neural codes for smooth shapes, but rely on shape priors that fail on new objects. ParCo-SDF instead mixes time shape coding with FiLM-tuned forecasts, with no shape priors. The time encoder captures likeness across runs, for prior-free training, while FiLM tuning preserves range and reduces size. Against a rival on a rubber band dataset, it shows robust rebuilds when much is hidden.
arxiv-2605-29617: R. Kiefe and J. S. Amaral present a multi-scale finite-temperature micromagnetic model joining Landau-Lifshitz and Bernoulli equations. The LLBe model reproduces classic Maxwell magnetostatics for paramagnets when hot and standard models for ferromagnets. By design it couples atomic-scale simulations with micromagnetics, giving consistent bulk predictions from below to above the Curie point. Validation runs against solvers cover zero-heat models and hot magnetostatics. A heat-assisted recording simulation on a thin track with local heating shows the model's multi-scale reach.
arxiv-2605-29917: Alisson dos Passos Fumaco and four colleagues test whether FALQON parameters transfer for Max-Cut across graph families. They move parameter sequences from small donors to fourteen-node recipients, using three-regular and Erdős-Rényi families. Success turns on the recipient, not the donor: dense recipients reach high ratios regardless of donor, while sparse cross-family cases stay challenging. Performance resists donor size, with eight-node donors matching larger ones. Cheap small graphs can supply robust parameters for larger targets, cutting measurement overhead in the feedback loop.
arxiv-2605-30117: Haoyuan Shi and eleven colleagues present VLA-Trace, a diagnostic framework for vision-language-action robot control models. It traces one evidence chain from shifting representations to causal control links and outward behaviour. Kernel alignment tracks drift, attention knockout maps pathways, and rollout probes test grounding, shortcuts and semantic following. Tests on two models reveal distinct adaptation patterns, different routing and layer links. Both models ground trajectories well in vision but follow fine-grained meaning poorly. The findings point toward adaptation that preserves representations, causal circuits and compositional semantic control.
arxiv-2605-30217: Sameer Dambal, Michael AD Taylor and Yu Zhang show how partial quantum error correction turns logical noise into a programmable resource for open simulations. Noise usually fights quantum information, yet open systems need dissipation. Treating fault-tolerant rounds as programmable units, decoder and recovery randomization generate controllable logical channels whose mixtures realize Kraus-channel mixing. Target dissipators can thus be compiled into logical dynamics without extra ancilla qubits for the bath. An accuracy criterion ties code distance to keeping uncontrolled errors a small fraction of intended dissipation.
arxiv-2605-30717: You, Nikeghbal, and Diesner study gender-specific neurons across feminine, masculine, and neutral categories. Prior work views gender as binary, with little attention to neutral forms like they pronouns. Their neuron-level method finds neurons tied to each gender category. Tests follow: activating or masking gender neurons steers a sentence toward a gender form while preserving meaning. Experiments on two open models show gender neurons concentrate in the earliest layers, with smaller contributions later. Their method achieves tighter gender control, with less leakage into non-target categories.
arxiv-2605-31117: Ochsner and Pampel propose requirements for a joint system for keeping research blogs digital. Access and reuse of knowledge is central to Open Science, yet prior work focused on old outputs. Research blogs, a medium for sharing research, have got little notice, risking information loss and a gap in the research record. Based on a mixed-methods design with hundreds of German blogs, talks, and an open review, they propose a catalog of needs. These needs bring blogs into systems to ensure long-term access, reuse, and citing.
arxiv-2605-31317: Dolgova and Stich study local collateral forgetting in machine unlearning. Standard tests boil unlearning quality to overall metrics, hiding local failures. Unlearned guesses versus a retrained model show per-case gaps vary wildly. Gradient-ascent and random-tagging methods show gaps growing near the forget set. Stand-in targets can clash with the local guess structure, spreading through shared codes to nearby examples. Local Teacher Distillation swaps random targets for soft labels from a teacher taught only on kept nearby cases. It closes the gap on CIFAR-100 deletion.
arxiv-2605-31417: Fischer and Habib revisit the Binary Closest String problem: given a set of binary strings, find a string cutting the maximum Hamming distance to the set. Prior tuned algorithms for the optimal distance improved from base d down through bases 16, 10, 8 and 7 to the best-known base 5. The authors present a faster chance-based algorithm with base 4. Their result meets a recent fine-grained lower bound and is therefore optimal on current proofs. As an extra benefit, the algorithm is very simple.

arxiv-2606-04217:
Boka Qin and Rui Yang release in 2026 the complete on-chain trade archive of Polymarket's first-generation exchange, a prediction market where users bet on event outcomes. The record covers November 2022 to April 2026: about a billion trades across well over a million markets.

Its special value is ground truth: the blockchain settlement layer records which side initiated each trade, something other archives only guess. Benchmarking the standard guessing rules against this truth, the pair found near-coin-flip accuracy overall, hiding a systematic, fixable error pattern tied to price level. Those errors flow into common market-health metrics and bias them. True measures of informed trading also predicted forecasting quality in ways the guessed proxies could not recover, a caution for market design research.
arxiv-2606-04317:
Bin Duan, Zeyu Bai, and Guowei Yang present ParDef in 2026, a defense for neural networks whose stored parameters, not their inputs, are attacked. Models now travel through cloud storage, build pipelines, and edge platforms, and tampered weights silently corrupt every later prediction.

Existing defenses retrain the model, cost accuracy, or cover only one attack style, while real attacks arrive in unpredictable forms: sparse edits, continuous shifts, or structured damage. ParDef layers three protections: keyed channel reparameterization to hide sensitive directions, error-correcting-code quantization to embed redundancy, and robust inference that stays stable under uncertainty. On three image benchmarks with two standard architectures, it cut attack success across all parameter attack types while keeping accuracy high and overhead moderate.
arxiv-2606-04717:
Tai audits a popular interpretability technique and shows its usual reading is unsound, in a 2026 arXiv paper on language model internals. Chain-of-thought hijack templates can flip a model's final numeric answer on math problems while the visible reasoning still looks fluent. Tai shows clean-only localization profiles underidentify the true source contrast.

He instead builds an audit that issues source-control certificates with a pre-registered Type-I error guarantee. The audit selects a candidate band with permutation calibration, freezes the hook, then runs paired-bootstrap source contrasts, with the error probability controlled by design. On Qwen2.5-7B and Llama3-8B, some cells pass confirmatory localization, with fixed-hook reruns recovering 47 percent and 39 percent of answers on puzzle sets, and 26 percent transfer on MATH-500. He stresses the method is a diagnostic auditing protocol, not a safety defense.
arxiv-2606-04817:
Saha Roy and Lacalle study how a peculiar kind of quantum error affects Grover's search algorithm, in a 2026 arXiv quantum computing paper. Isotropic errors are known to resist error correction, and general frameworks exist to model them, but their concrete impact on practical algorithms was unstudied. Grover's algorithm, the famous quantum search speedup, makes a clean test case. Through simulations, the authors analyze how isotropic errors change the algorithm's complexity, performance, and success probability.

The results give insight into the robustness of Grover's algorithm against this error type and highlight challenges. The library, simulation code, and documentation are online. The study matters because error correction cannot simply be assumed to clean up isotropic noise. Algorithm designers need to know how much success probability survives when this correction-resistant error is present in near-term devices.
arxiv-2606-04917:
Buzaglo and Rogalski classify the symmetries of a family of noncommutative polynomial rings, in a 2026 arXiv algebra paper. A Hopf algebra coaction is a generalized symmetry action on such a ring. The authors classify which cocommutative Hopf algebras coact inner-faithfully on the one-parameter skew polynomial rings in two and three variables. Their tool is Manin's universal coacting Hopf algebra, the master symmetry object from which all coactions descend.

Classifying its cocommutative quotients yields the classification, and as a direct corollary they obtain all group gradings on two- and three-variable skew polynomial rings. They also give an explicit presentation of the universal coacting algebra for arbitrary parameter and any number of variables. Classification results like this map the full symmetry landscape of quantum polynomial rings, staples of noncommutative geometry.
arxiv-2606-05617:
Alshahrani speeds up a solver for multi-goal convex problems in a 2026 arXiv paper. Vector optimization seeks points where no goal can improve without hurting another. A known outer method checks every corner of a shrinking shape estimate each round. It then keeps only the single best cut, wasting the rest of the work. Alshahrani changes both habits at once.

First, the corner checks run in parallel across many workers, cutting the time per round. Second, each round now adds a batch of cuts, one from each solved subproblem. The author proves the batch version keeps the same convergence rate as the standard method. On eight test problems with two to five goals, parallel runs on eight cores ran up to about four times faster. Batch cutting shrank the round count by sixty-two to eighty percent. Gains in clock time, though, depended on how costly each corner check was.
arxiv-2606-05717:
Shubham Gupta and colleagues caption sounds with a compact model fed by tag hints in a 2026 arXiv paper. Audio captioning writes sentences for acoustic scenes, like a busy street or a quiet kitchen. Giant sequence models do it well but are costly to run. Word choice also drifts without grounding. The team grounds a small decoder in predicted keywords from the AudioSet label bank.

Sound features come from a ConvNeXt encoder, read frame by frame. The top predicted keywords join those features as structured cues. A six-layer BART-style decoder then writes the caption from the joint signal. No large language model takes part in decoding. On the Clotho V2 and AudioCaps benchmarks, caption quality stayed competitive with far larger systems. The design targets real deployment limits, where small and fast matters. Code and trained models are public for reuse.
arxiv-2606-06117:
Tirtharaj Dash and Gunja Sachdeva introduce pVR in this 2026 arXiv paper on classifying DNA sequences without aligning them first. Their method uses p-adic numbers, a number system where closeness reflects shared prefixes. Each sequence is encoded twice: once by p-adic distances between short word prefixes, and once by how often those short words appear. Feeding both distances into one filtered shape summary gives features for ordinary classifiers.

The paper proves the construction is stable under small distance changes and independent of which prime is chosen. It also explains why one p-adic axis alone carries no useful shape information, while pairing the two recovers real structure. On twelve benchmarks, pVR beat four established alignment-free methods on three of six small datasets, with gains reaching twenty-one percentage points, though it lagged on a SARS-CoV-2 variant set.
arxiv-2606-06317:
Yonglei Yan and Zhengyang Liu study a classic market equilibrium in this 2026 arXiv paper on matching theory. The Hylland Zeckhauser scheme assigns goods to agents through prices, balancing fairness and efficiency. It is well understood when agents value goods at only two levels. Real markets have many value levels, and both computation and the shape of exact solutions become murkier there.

The authors give a polynomial time algorithm that finds an equilibrium within an additive error below one over e for general multi valued utilities. It is the first constant error guarantee of its kind for this setting. Their trick stratifies utilities, embedding the market into a structured two valued instance where an exact algorithm by Vazirani and Yannakakis applies. The second result is a warning: with just three value levels, a five by five market already forces every exact equilibrium to use irrational prices.
arxiv-2606-06417:
Caoilte Ó Ciardha and co-authors test how warning wording steers people toward help in this 2026 arXiv paper on online safety. When users of Ahmia.fi, a Tor search engine, searched for terms linked to child sexual abuse material, a warning page offered a link to an anonymous self help program. Which wording works best was unknown at real world scale, especially in a high anonymity setting. The team ran a field experiment over one hundred forty days.

Nearly twenty million searches were observed, and over three million triggered a warning. Messages varied in theme and framing, against a neutral control. Every active message raised click through to help resources over the neutral one. A harm focused message performed strongest. Across the platform, click through rose from eight point seven three percent before the campaign to fifteen point six seven percent during it.
arxiv-2606-06517:
Mushtaq Ahmad and co-authors ring an exotic black hole and listen for differences in this 2026 arXiv paper on modified gravity. In f of R T gravity, the action depends on curvature and on the trace of the matter stress energy. Here it takes a trace quadratic form. The black holes are held up by an anisotropic fluid, matter whose pressure differs by direction. The team studies odd parity perturbations, the axial wobbles behind gravitational wave ringdown.

First they map which fluid parameters allow a regular horizon and well behaved waves. The admissible branch needs a negative radial pressure parameter. The commonly used positive family fails regularity and survives only as a comparison. On good backgrounds the axial problem collapses to one master equation. For their anchored branch, the main ringdown mode's frequency shifts about twenty two percent from the Schwarzschild value, a potentially observable fingerprint.
arxiv-2606-06717:
AI drug design tools love deep pockets. Reddy and Liu point out that many prized cancer targets, such as KRAS and MYC, offer only shallow dents where a drug might grip. Their 2026 arXiv paper introduces ShallowBench, a benchmark built to expose that blind spot in generative models, the AI systems that invent new drug like molecules.

The benchmark holds five thousand seven hundred eighty targets drawn from a large public docking data set. To find genuinely shallow sites, the team compared two volumes. One sat under a fitted surface lid. The other was the volume of the protein atoms beneath it. They kept spots with low concavity but enough surface area. Top generative models produced molecules with weaker predicted binding on these flat interfaces than on deep pockets. The split into training and test targets used sequence similarity clustering, so test proteins stay clearly distinct from training ones.
arxiv-2606-06817:
Number a grid so that every four cycle face adds to the same total, and you have a magic labeling puzzle. Myers and Curran solve one such puzzle fully in this 2026 arXiv paper. Their board is a four by four grid drawn on a Klein bottle. A Klein bottle is a surface that loops back through itself.

Each vertex gets a distinct number from one to sixteen. Every square face must share one constant sum. The authors count all such labelings up to symmetry. There are exactly one hundred ninety two of them. They sort the labelings into two families. The split turns on how paired entries balance across rows or columns. In balanced cases, facing pairs each sum to seventeen. The work extends earlier results on Klein bottle grids of other sizes.
arxiv-2606-06917:
A wildfire sensor sees far more than its brief radio windows can send. Shao, Yamakawa, and Cheah Wai Shiang design the scheduling brain for that sensor in this 2026 arXiv paper. The receiver must predict a hazard map several steps ahead. It can only use whatever the sparse downlink delivered.

The authors frame the problem as scheduling under partial observation. Each region needs choices about sensing, representation, and transmission. A structured belief, a compact summary of what is known, guides those choices. They derive the belief from what the prediction task actually requires. Tests ran in a physics calibrated synthetic landscape. The winning belief component flipped between landscapes, showing the design tracks real structure. A tiny attention encoder with forty thousand parameters beat the reference method clearly. It improved results by about twenty eight percent on one landscape. Bigger transformer encoders added nothing but variance.
arxiv-2606-07017:
Agents that ace tidy benchmarks often stumble in the messy real world. Xiaoou Liu, Chen, Li, Hu, and Wei argue this is an old problem wearing new clothes in this 2026 arXiv paper. Robotics calls it the sim-to-real gap. A policy trained in simulation degrades on contact with reality. Foundation model agents, they claim, suffer the same disease.

Their framework sorts every failure through one classic lens. A Markov decision process has four parts: observation, action, transition, and reward. Each part can drift between training and deployment. A multilingual tool calling example makes the point sharply. The agent's intent is right, yet the action comes out invalid. The authors translate known remedies, like domain randomization, into agent terms. They call for shared vocabulary and standard stress test benchmarks. The paper is a research agenda, not a finished cure.
arxiv-2606-07117:
Most 3D scene generators secretly work in 2D, projecting shapes into pictures and back. Liu and co-authors at Kuaishou's GameMind Lab cut out that detour in this 2026 arXiv paper. Their Native3D framework generates indoor scenes end to end in three dimensions. No 2D intermediate representation appears anywhere in the pipeline.

A unified representation carries mesh geometry and texture together. A transformer encoder reads that joint code, preserving how objects sit relative to each other. A new alignment loss sharpens the marriage of shape and surface. It uses contrastive learning across several semantic levels in latent space. Experiments show gains in generation quality over prior methods. Editing flexibility improved as well. Users can add, remove, rearrange, or restyle objects in a scene. Multi view consistency, a common failure of projection based tools, came out strongest here.
arxiv-2606-07217:
Teaching a robot a new task usually means collecting labeled demonstrations and retraining its control model. Bianchi and co-authors propose skipping that step in this 2026 arXiv paper, with a framework called WIZARD. Their base models are vision-language-action systems, which link images and instructions to robot movements. WIZARD instead learns in weight space: it predicts the small parameter changes a task requires.

Given only a written instruction and a short demonstration video, WIZARD builds a compact adapter for the frozen base model in one pass. No action labels or test-time tuning are needed. That matters because a leading pretrained model scored zero success on one unseen LIBERO suite in their tests. The adapters raised success rates up to about twofold on average across unseen datasets, and far more on single tasks. Warm-starting later fine-tuning from these adapters also worked well.
arxiv-2606-07317:
Matveev and co-authors speed up recommendation systems that read very long user histories in this 2026 arXiv paper presented at a major information retrieval conference.
